text:
Alex: Quick Q for product — can we recalibrate RICE for the Q2 roadmap? Infra cost updates bumped effort on GPU-heavy items, so some scores will shift.
Maya: +1. We should also agree an "impact threshold" so we don't ship lots of tiny wins that eat bandwith.
Sam: @Alex can you drop the updated effort numbers? heard GPU ops estimates +30% across the board.
Alex: Uploaded a working sheet (internal): https://intranet.redwood/roadmaps/q2-rice-recalc — key candidates: dedicated-autoscale, adaptive-routing, streaming-latency improvements.
Devon: For context, my proposed numbers for Dedicated Autoscale:
```
Reach: 10,000 MAUs
Impact: 3 (medium-high)
Confidence: 0.7
Effort: 30 dev-weeks
RICE = (10000 * 3 * 0.7) / 30 = 700
```
That one still looks strong even with higher effort.
Priya: Heads-up: Private deployment/compliance gating reduces effective reach if we can't certify on time. If rollout delayed 6 weeks, reach can drop ~40% — adjust reach in the sheet accordingly.
Ethan: Sequence matter: streaming-latency -> adaptive-routing -> autoscale. Autoscale relies on routing infra; flipping order will block autoscale delivery.
Sam: Also strong launch gate suggestion: perf CI must pass `p95 < 120ms` and cost/unit under `$0.02` for public rollout, otherwise fallback to smaller model/limited rollout.
Maya: :thumbsup: Agree on gates. Also propose an "impact floor" — drop items with RICE < 20 unless strategic or customer-blocking.
Alex: OK — if we add that impact floor and apply the new effort multipliers, a few things drop (e.g., docs-search relevance tweak falls below threshold).
roadmap-bot: roadmap-bot: updated roadmap view + recalculated RICE column. View: https://intranet.redwood/roadmaps/q2-rice-recalc/view
Devon: One more rule proposal: weight customer-driven asks by x1.5 to Impact if NPS or CSAT indicates >9 for that use-case.
Priya: Fine but cap multiplier at 1.5 and require a named customer or >3 distinct customers asking — avoid gaming the multiplier.
Alex: Action items: (1) Alex to re-run sheet with impact floor=20 + customer multiplier rules, (2) Eng (Sam/Ethan) to verify updated effort estimates by EOD Tue, (3) Product (Maya/Devon/Priya) to mark rollout gates in tickets. Any objections?
Ethan: No objections. I'll add sequencing as a hard constraint on the epic tickets.
Sam: I'll add the perf CI checks and cost gating to the pipeline and report failures to #eng-oncall. :robot_face:
Alex: Thanks team — I'll post the final recalculated list here once done.
